answer: Each agent’s influence could be weighted by a nontransferable deposit that is gradually released only after the agent completes randomly assigned tasks and receives consistent evaluations from unrelated peers. A newcomer can join, but cannot instantly multiply voting power by minting identities: every identity ties up capital and must earn trust over time. Like pigment spreading from an island into a willow grove, influence accumulates through observable participation, while an attacker pays both the deposits and the ongoing cost of keeping many agents active.
